title: From Rice Baskets to Runway Bags: Young Hands Keep Bamboo Weaving Alive
title_zh: 从米篮到秀场包：年轻双手让竹编技艺延续
intro_zh: 本文约 523 词，难度适合 CET-4 阅读训练，围绕四川青神竹编技艺的传承与创新展开，包含具体事例与数据。

paragraphs.en: In a small workshop in Qingshen, Sichuan, the air smells of fresh bamboo. An old craftsman named Chen splits a green pole into thin strips. His hands move quickly and steadily. For more than 40 years, Chen has made baskets, fans and mats from bamboo. Qingshen bamboo weaving is over 2,000 years old and was listed as a national cultural heritage in 2008.
paragraphs.zh: 在四川青神的一间小作坊里，空气中弥漫着新鲜竹子的气味。一位名叫陈的老匠人把一根青竹劈成细条。他的双手动作又快又稳。四十多年来，陈一直用竹子制作篮子、扇子和席子。青神竹编已有两千多年历史，并于2008年被列为国家级文化遗产。

paragraphs.en: For a long time, however, the craft faced a serious problem. Young people left the village for city jobs, and few wanted to spend months learning such intricate skills. 'It takes three years just to master the basics,' Chen says. 'Many of my old students gave up.' By 2010, the number of full-time weavers in the town had fallen by half.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，很长一段时间里，这门手艺面临一个严重问题。年轻人离开村子去城市找工作，很少有人愿意花几个月学习如此复杂精细的技艺。“仅仅掌握基础就要三年，”陈说，“我以前的很多学生都放弃了。”到2010年，镇上全职编织者的数量已经减少了一半。

paragraphs.en: Then something changed. In 2015, a local training center opened its doors to young apprentices. The center offered free lessons and a small monthly payment. It also invited designers from big cities to work with the old masters. The idea was simple: keep the traditional methods, but find new uses for them.
paragraphs.zh: 后来情况发生了变化。2015年，当地一家培训中心向年轻学徒敞开大门。该中心提供免费课程和少量月度补贴。它还邀请大城市的设师与老匠人合作。想法很简单：保留传统方法，但为它们找到新用途。

paragraphs.en: One of the first students was Liu Yan, a 24-year-old art graduate. She spent three months learning to weave a single tea tray. The first one took her 90 days. 'At first I thought it was just a craft,' she says. 'Later I saw it as a language.' Liu and Chen now work together. Chen makes the base, and Liu adds modern patterns and colors.
paragraphs.zh: 最早的学生之一是24岁的艺术毕业生刘燕。她花了三个月学习编织一个茶盘。第一个茶盘花了她90天。“起初我以为它只是一门手艺，”她说，“后来我把它看作一种语言。”如今刘燕和陈一起工作。陈制作底座，刘燕加入现代图案和色彩。

paragraphs.en: Their first product was a handbag. It combined fine bamboo strips with leather handles. The bag was light, strong and beautiful. In 2018, it appeared at a design show in Paris. Orders soon came from Japan, Germany and the United States. Today, the town's bamboo exports reach more than 50 countries. The bags sell for 300 to 800 yuan each.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的第一款产品是一款手袋。它把精细的竹条和皮革手柄结合在一起。这款包轻便、结实又美观。2018年，它出现在巴黎的一场设计展上。订单很快从日本、德国和美国传来。如今，该镇的竹制品出口到五十多个国家。这些包每只售价300到800元。

paragraphs.en: The success is not only about money. Bamboo is a highly sustainable material. It grows back in three to five years, much faster than trees. It needs little water and no chemicals. For a world worried about plastic waste, bamboo weaving offers a green alternative. 'Every product we make replaces something made of plastic,' Liu says.
paragraphs.zh: 成功不仅仅在于钱。竹子是一种高度可持续的材料。它三到五年就能重新长成，比树木快得多。它需要的水很少，也不需要化学品。对于担心塑料垃圾的世界来说，竹编提供了一种绿色替代方案。“我们制作的每件产品都在替代某种塑料制品，”刘燕说。

paragraphs.en: Young people are also changing how the craft is sold. They use short videos to show each step: splitting, dyeing, weaving. Online orders now make up nearly 40 percent of total sales. 'Our customers want to know who made the product,' says Liu. 'A short video builds trust faster than a long advertisement.' Innovation, it seems, is part of tradition too.
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人也在改变这门手艺的销售方式。他们用短视频展示每一步：劈竹、染色、编织。如今，线上订单占总销售额的近40%。“我们的顾客想知道产品是谁做的，”刘燕说，“短视频比长篇广告更快建立信任。”看来，创新也是传统的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Still, the road is not easy. Machine-made products are cheaper and faster. Some young people leave after a few months. To preserve the craft, the local government now helps with marketing and provides health insurance for full-time weavers. Schools also invite craftsmen to give demonstrations. 'We need young people to see a future here,' Chen says.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，这条路并不容易。机器制品更便宜、更快。一些年轻人几个月后就离开了。为了保护这门手艺，当地政府如今帮助做市场推广，并为全职编织者提供医疗保险。学校也邀请匠人去做示范。“我们需要年轻人在这里看到未来，”陈说。

paragraphs.en: Back in the workshop, Chen is teaching a new student how to choose the right bamboo. The work is slow, but the room is full of young voices. Liu is designing a new lamp for an online store. The old craft is not frozen in a museum. It is alive, changing, and moving forward with the hands that touch it.
paragraphs.zh: 回到作坊里，陈正在教一名新学生如何挑选合适的竹子。工作很慢，但房间里充满了年轻人的声音。刘燕正在为一家网店设计一款新灯。这门古老手艺并没有被冻结在博物馆里。它活着，在变化，并随着触摸它的双手一起向前发展。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to grow bamboo in Sichuan.
The revival of a traditional bamboo weaving craft.
A famous design show in Paris.
questions.explain: 文章主要讲述青神竹编从面临人才断层到通过培训、设计和电商重新焕发生机的过程，因此B项“传统竹编技艺的复兴”最准确。

questions.q: According to the passage, what did the training center offer to young apprentices?
options: Free lessons and a small monthly payment.
Free bamboo and a city job.
questions.explain: 第三段明确提到培训中心提供免费课程和少量月度补贴，即free lessons and a small monthly payment。

questions.q: What can we infer about Liu Yan's attitude toward bamboo weaving?
options: She thinks it is too slow to be useful.
She believes it should be kept unchanged.
She sees it as a living art with new possibilities.
questions.explain: 刘燕把竹编看作一种语言，并与陈合作加入现代图案和色彩，还参与设计和电商销售，说明她认为竹编是活的、有新的可能，故选C。

questions.q: The word 'preserve' in paragraph 8 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: preserve意为“保护、保存”，与protect最接近；此处指保护竹编手艺不被遗忘或消失。
